The scheduler load balancer has specific code to deal with cases of
unbalanced system due to lots of unmovable tasks (for example because of
hard CPU affinity). In those situation
column2: it excludes the busiest CPU that

column1: has pinned tasks for load balance consideration such that it can perform
second 2nd load balance pass on the rest of the system.
This all works as designed if there is only one cgroup in the system.
However
column3: this logic has false positives and

column1: triggers multiple load balance passes despite there are actually no pinned
tasks at all.
The reason it has false positives is that the all pinned logic is deep in
the lowest function of can_migrate_task() and is too low level:
load_balance_fair() iterates each task group and calls balance_tasks() to
migrate target load. Along the way
all_pinned variable. Given that task-groups are iterated
variable is essentially the status of last group in the scanning process.
Task group can have number of reasons that no load being migrated
due to cpu affinity. However
column2: this status bit is being propagated back up

column1: to the higher level load_balance()
column2: which incorrectly think that no tasks

column1: were moved.  It kick off the all pinned logic and start multiple passes
attempt to move load onto puller CPU.
To fix this
column2: move the all_pinned aggregation up at the iterator level.

column1: This ensures that the status is aggregated over all task-groups
last one in the list.
